subject: Numeracy
title: Making patterns
objectives: Children will continue AB and AAB patterns.
Children will make their own pattern.
content: AB patterns, AAB and ABB patterns, and making my own pattern.
teachingActivities: Start with body patterns (clap, stamp) and sound patterns before objects; say the pattern aloud as you build it; use colour, shape and size; ask "What comes next?"; let children make their own and explain them.
learnerActivities: Continue AB and AAB patterns and make their own pattern.
assessment: Observe whether each child continues an AB pattern and makes a pattern of their own.
expectedOutcomes: Makes an AB or AAB pattern.

lessons.title: Body and sound patterns
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will copy and continue simple AB patterns with their bodies and sounds.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name five shapes, sort and order things.
lessons.starter: Clap, stamp, clap, stamp and say "This is a pattern. It repeats."
teacherActivities: Do a clap-stamp pattern and ask children to join.
Use the drum for a loud-soft pattern.
Let a child lead a pattern.
learnerActivities: Child says or does the next action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Do a clap-stamp pattern and ask children to join. Children: Children copy the pattern.
Step 2. Teacher: Stop and ask "What comes next?" Children: Child says or does the next action.
Step 3. Teacher: Use the drum for a loud-soft pattern. Children: Children copy the sounds.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead a pattern. Children: Child leads and friends copy.

practical.title: Clap and stamp
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear and the volume gentle. Make space for stamping.

differentiation.support: Do the pattern slowly and say each action.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a three-part pattern.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Do a last pattern and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Make clapping patterns with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "copy and continue simple AB patterns with their bodies and sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Colour patterns
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make and continue AB patterns with coloured objects.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name five shapes, sort and order things.
lessons.starter: Put red, blue, red, blue in a row and say "What comes next?"
teacherActivities: Make an AB pattern and say it aloud.
Let children make their own AB pattern.
learnerActivities: Children say red, blue, red, blue.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make an AB pattern and say it aloud. Children: Children say red, blue, red, blue.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What comes next?" Children: Child places the next cube.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children make their own AB pattern. Children: Child makes a pattern.
Step 4. Teacher: Check by saying the pattern. Children: Child says the pattern.

practical.title: Cube patterns
practical.safety: Use cubes larger than a fist or too big to swallow and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Continue a pattern that is already started.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a pattern with three colours.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the cubes away and say the pattern.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a pattern with socks or spoons at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make and continue AB patterns with coloured objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Longer patterns
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will continue AAB and ABB patterns.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name five shapes, sort and order things.
resources: Beads or cubes in two colours
lessons.starter: Put red, red, blue, red, red, blue and say "This pattern has two reds and one blue."
teacherActivities: Make an AAB pattern and say it aloud.
Let children continue patterns started by the teacher.
Introduce ABB with a new pattern.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make an AAB pattern and say it aloud. Children: Children say red, red, blue.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What comes next?" Children: Child says the next colour.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children continue patterns started by the teacher. Children: Child continues a pattern.
Step 4. Teacher: Introduce ABB with a new pattern. Children: Child says the pattern.

practical.title: Bead patterns
practical.safety: Use large wooden beads and supervise stringing so beads are not put in mouths. Keep strings short.

differentiation.support: Continue an AB pattern before trying AAB.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make an ABC pattern.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many reds in a row?

lessons.conclusion: Put the beads away and say the pattern.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a bead pattern at home with safe large beads.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "continue AAB and ABB patterns" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: My own pattern
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make their own pattern and explain it to a friend.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name five shapes, sort and order things.
lessons.starter: Say "Today you are pattern makers. You can use shapes, leaves or colours."
teacherActivities: Show examples of patterns made with different objects.
Let each child choose objects and make a pattern.
Ask each child to explain their pattern.
Draw or stick the pattern on paper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show examples of patterns made with different objects. Children: Children look and talk.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child choose objects and make a pattern. Children: Child makes a pattern.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask each child to explain their pattern. Children: Child says their pattern.
Step 4. Teacher: Draw or stick the pattern on paper. Children: Child draws the pattern.

practical.title: Pattern makers
practical.safety: Use clean leaves and smooth stones and wash hands afterwards. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Make the pattern together and name each object.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a pattern with two changes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Display the patterns and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for patterns at home such as on cloth or tiles.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make their own pattern and explain it to a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 patterns check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child makes and continues patterns.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name five shapes, sort and order things.
lessons.starter: Sing the pattern song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: cubes, beads and shapes.
At each station ask "What comes next?"
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: cubes, beads and shapes. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What comes next?" Children: Child continues a pattern.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Pattern stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large beads and cubes. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use AB patterns.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to make an ABC pattern.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: copies a pattern; continues an AB pattern; continues an AAB pattern; makes their own pattern.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
Makes and continues patterns with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child makes and continues patterns" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
